title: Detox: testing a React Native app

videos.script: Many apps are not written in Kotlin at all. They are written once, in JavaScript, with React Native, and run on Android and iOS. {{one-codebase}} Testing one of those with Espresso would mean testing the framework rather than the app. Detox was built for exactly this case. {{detox}} Detox is gray box, like Espresso. It sits inside the app, and before every tap it waits until the app is idle. {{gray-box}} Idle means more than the main thread. It means no request in flight, no timer about to fire, no animation running, and nothing left for the JavaScript to do. {{idle}} In this lesson you make a small React Native version of Tickets. You install Detox beside it, and write a spec that taps a show. {{spec}} Then the failure that belongs to Detox alone. An app that is never idle, and a test that waits for it forever. {{hang}} No React Native app is built or run here. What you will see run is everything around it. {{honest}}
